Hi Lara / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful to understand BrightHealth AI's goals for clinical summarization and the latency constraints on the triage flow. Quick recap and suggested next steps: 

- Recap: you want a Hosted API trial to validate inference quality and latency on 1-2 endpoints (summarization and entity extraction). Expected pilot load: ~10-20 requests/sec peak, ~100k tokens/day.
- Security & data residency: you noted PII concerns and a SOC 2 + data retention requirement; we can provide our SOC 2 summary and discuss retention settings on Hosted.
- Quickstart: I attached a short Quickstart guide with sample requests and a one-click sandbox key for the pilot.
- Rate limits & endpoints: Hosted API default limits are 60 requests/min per API key and burstable for pilot trials; for your scale we typically recommend a pilot key with 200 requests/min and token throttles configured.
- Next steps:
  1) Can you confirm which model/throughput we should pre-provision for the pilot (10 rps vs 20 rps)?
  2) Please share any compliance questionnaire items we should address up front.
  3) Pick a 45-min quickstart/demo slot next week and we'll provision a sandbox key + sample dataset.

I added Marissa (solutions) to the thread for a quick cost/throughput estimate and to handle the provisioning.

Best,

Thanks Aditya — great meeting. Quick answers from our side: 

- Pilot profile: we want to start with Hosted API. Primary objective is quality & latency; if Hosted works we may move to Dedicated later for cost predictability. For the pilot please provision for the 20 rps peak so we can stress test.
- Security: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and details on short-term data retention (we cannot retain raw PII beyond 30 days). Please send the SOC 2 summary and your recommended retention settings for Hosted.
- Compliance questionnaire: I attached a short vendor security checklist we'll send if things look good.
- Quickstart slot: morning PST on May 10 or May 11 works for our engineering team.

Also: what are the sandbox key limits (tokens/min and requests/sec) and are streaming responses supported on the Hosted API?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Lara —

Sharing the specifics you asked for and a couple of configuration suggestions: 

- SOC 2 & retention: attached is our SOC 2 summary. Hosted API supports configurable retention windows per account; we can set a 30-day retention policy for your pilot and provide audit logs for queries. (See attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)

- Sandbox limits & streaming: the sandbox keys support streaming responses (server-sent events / chunked transfer). Default sandbox quota: 60 req/min and 100k tokens/day. For your requested pilot (20 rps peak) we recommend a provisional sandbox key with elevated throughput: 200 req/min and token caps at 500k/day to give headroom for testing. If you want sustained 20 rps, we can enable burst policies and monitor.

- Sample curl (Hosted API) — replace $KEY with the sandbox key we'll provision:

curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-bison-1","input":"Summarize the following clinical note...","max_tokens":256,"stream":true}'

- Throughput & scaling: if after pilot you need guaranteed baseline throughput and isolation, Dedicated capacity is the next step; we can provide an options doc during pilot. For now Hosted should be fine for evaluation.

I'll provision the elevated sandbox key once you confirm May 10 vs May 11 for the quickstart.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
